newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends mixed, losses trimmed late.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends mixed, losses trimmed late.

text.p: Losses posted during the session in the soy product pits were trimmed late by a modest rebound in soybean futures near the close, CBOT traders said.
Soymeal futures settled mixed and soyoil, lower.
Most of the late advances in both markets were linked to short covering by local traders, floor sources said.

Earlier weakness in soymeal futures had been tied to lackluster weekly export sales data. The U.S. Department of Agriculture reported soymeal sales of 40,800 tonnes, below expectations for 60,000 to 80,000 tonnes.
An expected drop in soymeal feed use in the Midwest because of warmer weather was also a bearish factor, trade sources said.
But nearby soyoil futures were underpinned by export data. USDA reported sales during the week ended Dec. 26 were a robust 63,900 tonnes.
Floor sources also noted active spread trading in both markets, they said.
CBOT soyoil futures settled down 0.20 to 0.02 cent per lb, with January down 0.02 at 23.01 cents. Soymeal settled down $0.80 a ton to up $1.20 with January down 0.80 at $227.80.

Some traders said a heavy weekly crushing pace also contributed to the weakness in soy product markets. The National Oilseed Processors Association reported Thursday that the crush was 30.58 million bushels, which was far above trade expectations for 29.0 to 29.8 million bushels.
On the day, Cargill sold 200 lots of January soymeal and ADM sold 100 lots March, traders said, while Dean Witter sold 200 lots March and Smith Barney bought 200 lots March.
In soyoil trading, Cargill sold 400 lots March and Smith Barney and Dean Witter each bought 250 lots March, sources said.

Soyoil futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 20,000 contracts, below the 23,007 traded Thursday. Soymeal futures volume was estimated at 18,500 contracts, below the 22,930 traded Thursday, the exchange said.
